Original Text: Half of all American adults have high blood pressure, also known as hypertension. Many don't even know it. High blood pressure develops when blood flows through your arteries at higher-than-normal pressures.
Simple Explanation: About half of adults in the U.S. have high blood pressure, which doctors also call hypertension. Many people who have it don't know they have it. High blood pressure means your blood is pushing through your blood vessels (arteries) harder than normal.
Source: NHLBI (National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH)

Original Text: Diabetes is a disease that occurs when your blood glucose, also called blood sugar, is too high. Glucose is your body's main source of energy. Your body can make glucose, but glucose also comes from the food you eat. Insulin is a hormone made by the pancreas that helps glucose get into your cells to be used for energy. If you have diabetes, your body doesn't make enough—or any—insulin, or doesn't use insulin properly.
Simple Explanation: Diabetes is a disease where there is too much sugar (glucose) in your blood. Your body uses this sugar as its main fuel. Some of it comes from food, and your body can also make it. Insulin is a hormone made by an organ called the pancreas. It helps sugar move from your blood into your cells so they can use it for energy. With diabetes, the body makes too little insulin, makes none at all, or can't use it the right way.
Source: NIDDK (National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, NIH)

Original Text: Asthma is a chronic (long-term) lung disease. It affects your airways, the tubes that carry air in and out of your lungs. When you have asthma, your airways can become inflamed and narrowed. This can cause wheezing, coughing, and tightness in your chest. When these symptoms get worse than usual, it is called an asthma attack or flare-up.
Simple Explanation: Asthma is a lung disease that lasts a long time. It affects your airways, which are the tubes that carry air into and out of your lungs. With asthma, these tubes can get swollen and narrow. This can cause wheezing (a whistling sound when you breathe), coughing, and a tight feeling in your chest. When these problems get worse than usual, it is called an asthma attack or flare-up.

Original Text: Dehydration is a condition caused by the loss of too much fluid from the body. It happens when you are losing more fluids than you are taking in. Dehydration can be mild, or it can be severe enough to be life-threatening.
Simple Explanation: Dehydration means your body has lost too much water and other fluids. It happens when more fluid leaves your body than you drink or take in. Dehydration can be mild, but it can also become serious enough to put your life in danger.

Original Text: The common cold is a mild infection of your upper respiratory tract (which includes your nose and throat). Colds are probably the most common illness. There is no cure for the common cold. But there are treatments that can make you feel better while you wait for the cold to go away on its own.
Simple Explanation: A cold is a mild infection of your nose and throat. Colds are probably the most common illness people get. There is no cure for a cold, but some treatments can help you feel better while the cold goes away by itself.
